items.titleEn: Nvidia faces US accounting probe amid deepening turmoil
items.summaryEn: This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility: U.S. securities regulators are investigating the accounting practices of Nvidia, according to U.S. media, adding to the turmoil engulfing the artificial intelligence chip giant following the resignation of its chief executive. The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) inquiry is in its early stages, The New York Times reported Saturday, citing people briefed on the confidential investigation.

items.titleEn: Will Jensen Huang's ouster push founders to secure more voting rights?
items.summaryEn: Buy Meta (META). If founders respond to Huang’s ouster by pushing for more control, the market will reward companies with proven, durable governance that already concentrates voting power (Zuckerberg’s dual-class). META’s structure reduces the chance of disruptive governance fights during leadership crises, supporting steadier execution and capital allocation. Key Risk: Regulators or investors successfully pressure Meta to unwind dual-class voting, or a major governance/legal event forces a structural change. Sell NVDA. The article frames Huang’s exit as a national-security/espionage narrative that governance (even dual-class) can’t fix. That keeps a credibility and execution overhang on the new leadership, even with strong near-term results. The market will keep discounting “key-person + investigation risk” until the probe outcome is clean.

items.titleEn: Gold falls toward $3,500, silver slides as stock markets enter correction territory - Kitco PM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) - Spot gold and silver prices were sharply lower in late U.S. trading Friday, extending their recent selloff as a historic technology-led equity market decline and expectations for additional Federal Reserve interest rate increases pressured precious metals. Gold approached the psychologically important $3,500 level, trading at its lowest prices since September 2025, while silver suffered even heavier losses amid concerns about industrial demand and deteriorating global risk sentiment. The metals failed to benefit from sharply lower Treasury yields as investors reduced exposure to commodities alongside equities. At 5 p.m. ET, spot gold was trading near $3,537.90 an ounce, down $86.30, or 2.38%, while silver was trading near $41.120, down $1.637, or 3.83%, on the session. Gold traded as low as $3,502.93 during the day, while silver touched $40.660. Friday's U.S. economic data offered some evidence of easing inflation expectations and improving consumer sentiment, although the figures provided little relief to precious metals amid the broader financial-market selloff. The University of Michigan's final November consumer sentiment index increased to 51.5 from 48.0 in October, a 7.3% monthly improvement and its highest reading since August. The current economic conditions index rose to 49.4 from 46.7, while the expectations index increased to 52.9 from 48.8. More significantly for monetary policy, consumers' one-year inflation expectations declined to 3.7% from 4.7% in October, while longer-term expectations eased to 3.3% from 3.5%. The improvement reflected some relief from falling gasoline prices and expectations for changes in economic policy following the midterm elections. However, concerns about artificial intelligence valuations and recent stock market losses continued to weigh on households with substantial financial assets. The figures followed Thursday's weaker jobless claims and Philadelphia Fed manufacturing reports, reinforcing the increasingly uneven outlook for economic growth and inflation.

items.titleEn: There are five trillion reasons not to give up on gold just yet
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - There is no denying that this week’s price action delivered a gut punch to gold and silver investors. But while the precious metals may be down, they are certainly not out. And there could be 5 trillion new reasons why gold prices rally in the months ahead. While rising bond yields and expectations of further Federal Reserve rate hikes have created significant headwinds for gold, the bigger picture remains unchanged. Gold continues to play an important role as a hedge against growing sovereign debt risks. In a report published Friday, as gold prices tested support at $3,500, CIBC Capital Markets warned that the U.S. government could hit its $41.1 trillion debt ceiling as early as late February, setting up another contentious political showdown in Washington. The report might not make major headlines, but it provides a glimmer of light on a dark day. The bank estimates that Congress may eventually need to raise the debt ceiling by nearly $5 trillion to provide enough borrowing capacity through the 2028 elections. That is an extraordinary amount of money, even by Washington's increasingly extravagant spending standards. The bigger question is what another massive increase in the debt ceiling means for confidence in U.S. government debt and the U.S. dollar. We saw a glimpse of this dynamic in August, when gold rallied as the Treasury announced an expanded debt buyback program. Although designed to support market liquidity, the program highlighted the growing challenges of managing America's enormous debt burden. A $5 trillion increase in borrowing authority could bring those concerns back into focus. Société Générale is already positioning for this possibility. In its latest multi-asset outlook, the French bank identified the approaching debt ceiling as a potential catalyst for renewed dollar weakness and higher gold prices. SocGen maintained its 10% portfolio allocation to gold and continues to recommend buying price dips. The bank expects gold to reach $5,000 an ounce by the end of 2027. Of course, another debt ceiling confrontation could initially create liquidity pressures that weigh on gold, particularly if investors are forced to raise cash. But that would not undermine the longer-term investment case. The Federal Reserve can raise interest rates to fight inflation, but monetary policy cannot solve Washington's structural debt problem. Gold doesn't need a sovereign debt crisis to thrive. It only needs investors to question how much longer the current fiscal trajectory can continue. And with another $5 trillion potentially on the horizon, that question isn't going away.

items.titleEn: Wall Street stays bearish after gold's slide to $3,500, Main Street pessimism deepens ahead of holiday week
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) – Gold prices suffered another brutal weekly decline as increasingly hawkish Federal Reserve rate expectations, surging Treasury yields, and a stronger U.S. dollar overwhelmed safe-haven demand, while a deepening technology-led equity selloff triggered widespread liquidations and drove the precious metal to its lowest level in over a year. Spot gold kicked off the week trading at $3,869.30 per ounce on Sunday evening, and the yellow metal briefly attempted to stabilize following the previous week's sharp decline, with prices setting their weekly high at $3,901.40 per ounce on Monday. But the recovery quickly faded as markets continued to price in another Fed rate hike in December, while persistent inflation concerns and lingering tensions surrounding Iran and the Strait of Hormuz provided little support. Selling pressure intensified Tuesday after October retail sales rose just 0.2%, while stronger core spending failed to ease concerns about inflation. Gold broke decisively below $3,800 on Wednesday as the dollar strengthened, and the decline accelerated after the minutes from the Fed's October meeting showed policymakers remained firmly committed to further tightening, with some officials considering a larger 50-basis-point increase in December.

items.titleEn: Gold and silver suffer brutal losses as liquidity crunch deepens, but analysts see signs of a bottom
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Liquidity demands are once again punishing gold and silver , with both precious metals seeing their worst weekly declines since March as investors scramble to raise cash amid growing turmoil in global equity markets. Gold prices are down roughly 9.5% this week as they test critical support at $3,500 an ounce. At the same time, silver prices have fallen more than 15%, testing support around $41 an ounce. Silver is seeing its worst week since the start of the year as prices continue to sell off from their record highs near $120 an ounce. Analysts note that gold and silver have been hit by a tidal wave of selling as major equity indices drop on growing fears surrounding the artificial intelligence sector and potential pushback against data center buildouts. Analysts explained that the robust liquidity of gold and silver make them go-to assets for investors who need to raise capital to protect their portfolios.

items.titleEn: Gold and silver could return to mid-2025 levels as inflation-hedge bid evaporates – SIA's Cieszynski
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) – Gold ’s role as an inflation hedge is beginning to work against it as energy prices fall and as a new Congress looks to curtail the administration’s trade tariffs, and the yellow metal is likely to return to the base that launched last year’s parabolic rally, according to Colin Cieszynski, chief market strategist at SIA Wealth Management. Cieszynski noted the massive drop in inflation expectations in the University of Michigan’s consumer sentiment survey on Friday morning, and he said he believes it’s a major driver of gold’s weakness in the session. “I think that's why we're seeing gold come off as much as we are,” he said. “It's not so much the political side; I'm thinking it's more the inflation side, gold as a hedge against inflation.”
